svg.title: Five chokepoint types compared by capability, placement and what each one cannot do
svg.desc: A stateless ACL filters five-tuples at line rate but tracks no session and sees no application. A stateful firewall tracks sessions, translates addresses and identifies applications, but its state must be synchronised across an HA pair. An IPS detects and blocks known attacks on north-south paths but is blind to encrypted traffic and needs tuning. A WAF covers HTTP attacks on published applications only. A proxy or CASB controls and audits outbound access but needs endpoint cooperation. The three hard constraints are few and explicit chokepoints, accepting the encryption and inspection conflict, and synchronising state.
svg.text: Not every crossing deserves the same device
Pick the chokepoint by what it must decide — then write down what it will be blind to
CHOKEPOINT
WHAT IT DECIDES
WHERE IT BELONGS
WHAT IT CANNOT DO
stateless ACL / iACL
line rate, no memory
five-tuple permit or deny, at wire speed
cheap, deterministic, no session table to exhaust
coarse filtering inside a domain,
infrastructure and loopback protection
tracks no session and identifies no application;
it cannot tell a browser from a backup
stateful firewall
every main crossing
sessions, NAT, application identification
the default answer for inter-domain paths
every main inter-domain path,
in pairs, sized for peak sessions
keeps state: an HA pair that does not sync
sessions drops every long-lived connection at failover
IPS
known attacks
signature detection and blocking
known bad, at the cost of false positives
north-south main paths,
data centre ingress, mail and web edges
blind inside IPsec and TLS; needs decryption
at the chokepoint, and continuous tuning
WAF
HTTP only
HTTP-layer attacks: injection, scripting, bots
understands the protocol, so it can be precise
application front ends that are
published to the Internet
covers web only; it has no opinion about
a database port or an MQTT broker
proxy / CASB
who goes out
outbound control, audit, data loss rules
the only place that sees user to SaaS traffic
Internet egress,
SaaS access and shadow IT discovery
needs the endpoint to cooperate: proxy settings,
PAC file or an agent; bypass is one setting away
Three constraints that decide whether this design survives contact with operations
few and explicit
traffic must converge, or consistency and
capacity planning both become impossible
encryption against inspection
terminate at the chokepoint, or accept the
segment is unobservable — write down which
state must survive failover
otherwise the switchover succeeds and the
business stops: the worst kind of success
